title: Vanishing & Exploding Gradients — Repeated Multiplication Changes Scale
key_insight: Activation slopes and weight scales therefore matter across depth. Careful initialization keeps forward signals and backward gradients in a workable range.
body:
## Repeated Multiplication Changes Scale

A backward signal passes through many slopes. Multiplying repeatedly by numbers below one shrinks it; multiplying by numbers above one grows it.

Activation slopes and weight scales therefore matter across depth. Careful initialization keeps forward signals and backward gradients in a workable range.

ReLU-like activations avoid the flat ends of sigmoid for positive inputs, though they introduce their own inactive-unit risk.
common_mistakes: Vanishing gradients make every update infinitely large.
Gradient clipping creates new labels for the dataset.
Depth can never affect backward signal scale.
mini_exercise: Sketch the situation in “Repeated Multiplication Changes Scale” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Unhealthy gradient scale prevents early layers from learning and can make training numerically unstable.
